title: Idempotent reservation requests
summary: Store each request’s input and outcome in the same critical section as the seat allocation.
code: raise ValueError("key reused with different seats")
receipt = None  # Sold out is also an outcome.
triggers: client retries a write after losing the response
idempotency key must bind to the original request payload
prompts: A reservation succeeded, but the response was lost. Make its retry return the original receipt without taking more seats.
Reject a retry that uses the same key with a different seat count, even when there is enough capacity.
invariant: Each key stores one seat count and outcome. Looking up the key, allocating seats, and saving the result are one locked operation.
mantra: Look up, verify, apply once, replay.
pitfalls: Checking capacity before replay can reject a duplicate of the request that filled the venue.
A lock only protects this process. Persist both the effect and the outcome in one transaction to survive restarts or multiple processes.
A real service needs a retention policy and should scope keys to the caller and operation.

anchors.name: Lost response
anchors.trick: Replay the saved outcome before evaluating current capacity.

anchors.name: Concurrent duplicates
anchors.trick: The duplicate must observe either the whole committed result or no record.

mutations.replacement: if key in self._receipts and seats <= self._remaining:
mutations.explanation: Replay now depends on current capacity, so a retry can lose its original receipt.
